thread:
maria: Heads-up — saw a spike of ~6M late telemetry events from eu-prod (ingest delay). Aggregates are stale for ~4h windows. I think we should try a stitching + shallow-recompute approach instead of full backfill to avoid blowing quotas.
kevin: +1 to avoiding a full recompute. What do you mean by "stitching" here? map event_ids to existing rows and only replay affected partitions?
maria: Exactly. Two steps: 1) event_id remap / dedupe pass to mark which aggregates changed, 2) shallow recompute that recalculates only those time-shards. Should be much cheaper.
devon: How do we handle KV cache invalidation for prefix caching? If we recompute a shard we need to invalidate related prefixes or dashboards will show inconsistent spikes.
alex: We can emit a reprocess invalidation marker to the cache service. Proposed tag: reproc:{job_id}:{shard}. Cache listens and expires keys with that tag. Low overhead.
tara: Quotas: ops wants to cap concurrent recompute tokens per org. We need a circuit-breaker in the backfill coordinator so tenant-heavy customers don't starve normal traffic.
maria: Agreed. Suggest default concurrency 3 per-tenant, configurable. Also add a global throttle that keeps token-based throughput under SLA.
kevin: API surface: do we add a new internal endpoint POST /v1/telemetry/recompute? Needs dry-run and preview mode so we can surface cost estimates in Console.
devon: Preview mode is critical. Also the endpoint must be idempotent and return a job_id. We should record estimated token-cost and shard-count in job metadata.
ops-bot: New job queued: reproc-preview-2245123456 by maria (sandbox). Link: https://ci.redwood/reprocs/2245123456
alex: UX in Console: show a progress bar, affected dashboards list, and an escape hatch to pause/cancel. Can we also surface the expected SLO impact (estimated p95 latency increase)?
tara: For rollouts: canary recompute first for a 1% shard sample, compare metrics with golden set, then expand. That reduces blast radius.
maria: Good. We also need a repo change: update dedupe logic to prefer event_id+ingest_ts remap instead of only event_id, to fix reordering edge cases.
kevin: We should run a dry-run on staging with production-ish payload shape. Schedule overnight when ingestion is quiet.
devon: I'll sketch the coordinator changes: job planner that accepts a list of shards, computes affected partitions, estimates cost, and schedules token lease against quota service.
alex: I'll add cache invalidation handler and the Console UI mock. Maria/Tara can you draft the preview response fields we need? e.g. {job_id, shard_count, est_tokens, est_duration, canary_plan}
maria: Will do. I'll open an RFC PR with cost numbers and a sample curl for preview and submit modes. Example preview call:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/telemetry/recompute -d '{"start":"2026-03-15T00:00:00Z","end":"2026-03-15T04:00:00Z","mode":"preview","strategy":"stitch-shallow","canary_percent":1}'
```
kevin: Nice. Also add a flag to opt into strict mode that forces full recompute for customers that want absolute guarantees.
tara: Action items: Maria RFC, Devon coordinator patch, Alex cache + Console UI, Kevin add API contracts + idempotency tests. Ops will schedule a staging dry-run after initial PRs. I'll own tenant quota policy.
maria: Thanks — let's aim for a dry-run next week. Will tag folks in the RFC.
ops-bot: Noted: assignees set (maria, devon, alex, kevin, tara). Staging dry-run scheduled: 2026-03-22 02:00 UTC.
